person: Nadia Haddad is a 50-year-old part-time bookkeeper with a chronic spine condition who can sit at a screen for only about twenty minutes at a time. She pays her out-of-network therapist, Dr. Lena Brandt, up front every week and is reimbursed by the health plan through her part-time employer's group coverage. The claims are months behind, and she has lost track of which sessions were claimed, which were paid and which were paid wrong. She is also preparing for a second-opinion appointment in three weeks and managing her father's Medicare drug plan, so she wants this done in short, calm pieces, with honest statements of how sure any dollar figure is.
stated_up_front: I have about fifteen minutes today. My therapy reimbursements are months behind and I don't know which sessions were ever claimed. Can you sort it out and tell me what you need from me?

facts.truth: Dr. Lena Brandt, $165 per 50-minute session, weekly on Thursdays; a 30-minute session is billed at $110
Pays Dr. Brandt by debit card from her Ledgerline checking account on the day of each session
$750 out-of-network deductible per year; she believes it was met in March of this year
The plan pays 60% of its allowed amount for out-of-network therapy, which she understands to be $140 for a 50-minute session

facts.about: Old session she may have missed
facts.truth: A session in early September of last year that she does not remember ever claiming
Two joint sessions with her husband, Samir, in the spring, which the plan's terms exclude
One $80 fee in June when she cancelled for a pain flare; she knows it was not a real session
One 30-minute session in July that the office first coded as a full session; Dr. Brandt's office emailed her a corrected superbill
One claim for a session in May, submitted online in early July, with no answer since and no letter she remembers
Her father's Medicare drug plan is separate and not part of this; she does not want it touched
An email in her inbox from a company offering to fight her therapist's bills for 15% of whatever they recover; she has not answered it
She can work about 15-20 minutes at a stretch and wants to be able to stop and resume without redoing anything

unknowns: Whether the plan sent an extension notice on the overdue claim, since she doesn't read every plan email
How long she has to appeal a claim or file one, since she has never read the plan's rules
Whether the plan used this year's or last year's allowed amounts on any claim
Which of her claims were paid wrong, if any
Whether the surprise-billing law applies to a therapist she chose herself
